news.text: 8 August saw hundreds of thousands of university students, monks, and ordinary citizens take to the streets across Burma on **8-8-88**, launching the historic **8888 Uprising** against General Ne Win's authoritarian socialist regime. Demanding multi-party democratic governance and an end to crippling economic hardship, the demonstrators brought the capital of Rangoon to a complete standstill. The civilian protests brought future Nobel laureate **Aung San Suu Kyi** to international prominence, before being brutally crushed weeks later by a bloody military junta coup.

17 August saw Pakistani military dictator President **Muhammad Zia-ul-Haq** die in a mysterious aviation crash when his official C-130 Hercules aircraft plummeted into the desert near Bahawalpur shortly after takeoff. The disaster also killed thirty others aboard, including prominent senior Pakistani military generals and United States Ambassador Arnold Raphel. The abrupt demise of Zia, who had ruled Pakistan with an iron fist since his 1977 coup, paved the way for open democratic general elections and the historic election of Benazir Bhutto.

news.text: 20 August saw the guns fall silent across the Persian Gulf as the catastrophic **Iran-Iraq War** officially terminated with a UN-brokered ceasefire under United Nations Security Council Resolution 598. Spanning nearly eight years of brutal trench warfare, ballistic missile attacks against civilian cities and widespread chemical weapons usage, the conflict claimed an estimated one million lives with zero territorial adjustments for either nation. Both Saddam Hussein and Ayatollah Khomeini claimed victory from the ruins, leaving behind devastated national treasuries.

news.text: 21 August saw British club vocalist **Yazz** and the Plastic Population reach number one on the UK singles chart with their stomping Hi-NRG acid-house anthem *The Only Way Is Up*. Produced by Coldcut and featuring infectious horn fanfares alongside a driving breakbeat, the euphoric track spent five consecutive weeks at number one, becoming the ultimate commercial anthem of Britain's **Second Summer of Love**. The single cemented acid house's transition from underground motorway raves straight into high street record shops.

news.text: 29 August saw the World Wrestling Federation inaugurate **SummerSlam** before a roaring sell-out crowd at Madison Square Garden in New York City. The marquee main event saw the **Mega Powers** (WWF World Heavyweight Champion Randy Savage and Hulk Hogan) take on the "Mega Bucks" duo of Ted DiBiase and André the Giant, with special guest referee Jesse "The Body" Ventura. The climax saw Miss Elizabeth famously remove her red skirt to distract DiBiase and André, allowing Savage and Hogan to clear the ring and celebrate in theatrical triumph.

gaming.title: Altered Beast
gaming.reviewQuote: Terrifying transformations, thunderous digitized speech, and mythic carnage. A showcase of Sega's coin-op power.
gaming.headline: Rise from Your Grave: Lycanthropy in Ancient Greece
gaming.gameplay: Created by Makoto Uchida on Sega's formidable System 16 arcade board, *Altered Beast* opened with Zeus's booming, scratchy digitized declaration: **"Rise from your grave!"** Resurrected to rescue the goddess Athena from the demonic underworld lord Neff, players fought through waves of rotting zombies and flesh-eating demons. By defeating two-headed wolves and grabbing glowing Spirit Balls, the centurion warrior's muscles tore through his armor in a dramatic transformation sequence, morphing into a **Werewolf, Were-tiger, Were-bear, or Golden Werewolf** with screen-shredding energy charges.
gaming.reception: Debuting in arcades in August 1988, *Altered Beast* drew immense crowds with its digitized voice acting, gigantic character sprites, and visceral body-horror power-ups. Critics praised its audio-visual spectacle, and it quickly established itself as one of the definitive summer arcade attractions in British seaside resorts and American shopping malls.
gaming.impact: Uchida's arcade hit achieved legendary status when Sega made the brilliant strategic decision to bundle its 16-bit home conversion as the pack-in cartridge for the western launch of the Sega Genesis / Mega Drive in 1989. For millions of households, *Altered Beast* was their first jaw-dropping taste of 16-bit arcade perfection at home.
